title: m5stack/m5stack-linux-dtoverlays #19: fast key after a Sym/Aa/Fn tap consumes the layer; reported cases fixed, one pre-existing timeout window remains

execution.environment: macOS arm64; no Cardputer Zero hardware; local Device Service cardputer-zero profile supported=false creatable=false backend_ready=false (Linux ARM64 backend, __missing_qemu__/__missing_rom__); no Linux ARM64 kernel headers or cross toolchain for a module rebuild

checks.name: patch_scope
checks.evidence: 2 files, +54/-7, single commit e7f7a18: EV_OTHER_KEY_PRES + per-instance used, consume_layer(), WAIT dispatch on other-key release, timer update only on state change; evidence/pr-metadata.txt

checks.name: bug_reproduced_on_main
checks.evidence: host harness, pre-fix fsm: tap+fast key -> ONESHOT layer=1; chord (key up first) -> ONESHOT layer=1; evidence/host-harness-pre-fix.txt

checks.name: no_regression_oneshot_hold_lock_roll
checks.evidence: plain tap/pause/single-key, tap-and-wait, hold, double-tap lock/unlock, pre-held-key roll and locked-key-release outputs identical to main; evidence/host-harness.txt

checks.name: residual_wait_timeout_ignores_used
checks.evidence: PR head: KEY_PRES,KEY_RELE,OTHER_KEY_PRES,TIMEOUT_300 -> ONESHOT layer=1, so a key held past 300 ms (or still-held sibling key gating the all-released check) re-arms the layer; same result on main, pre-existing, not a regression; evidence/host-harness-residual-pr-head.txt

checks.name: residual_guard_proposal
checks.evidence: adding 'if (me->used) consume_layer(me);' to the WAIT timeout branch yields IDLE layer=0 for both residual sequences and leaves all baseline sequences identical; patches/0002; evidence/host-harness-residual-guarded.txt

checks.name: used_lifetime
checks.evidence: used is cleared on ST_ACTIVE entry and the object comes from devm_kzalloc() (tca8418_keypad_m5stack.c:767), so it starts at 0 and cannot leak across activation cycles

checks.name: timer_cancel_same_ordered_wq
checks.evidence: new tca8418_fsm_update_timer() call in the other-key-release path only fires on a state change and cancels an armed 300 ms work; keypad_data->wq is alloc_ordered_workqueue() (tca8418_keypad_m5stack.c:777), so the timeout work cannot execute concurrently with the IRQ work. Source-level reasoning only; no IRQ stress test.

checks.name: kernel_build_w1
checks.evidence: no Linux ARM64 kernel headers or cross toolchain on this host; the author reports an out-of-tree arm64 6.18 W=1 build, not re-run here

checks.name: hardware_validation
checks.evidence: no Cardputer Zero hardware on this host; the author's on-device result is self-reported and was not independently reproduced

checks.name: virtual_device_validation
checks.evidence: cardputer-zero profile supported=false creatable=false backend_ready=false, missing __missing_qemu__/__missing_rom__, reason 'CardputerZero uses a separate Linux backend'; evidence/local-profile-summary.txt

checks.name: timing_and_irq_batching
checks.evidence: harness drives ordered events; real 300 ms timer jitter, interrupt batch ordering and cancel/expiry races are unmeasured

checks.name: input_led_side_effects
checks.evidence: stubbed emit_*/led_* only count calls; real input event ordering and LED state are not observed

checks.name: ci_build
checks.evidence: the only PR check workflow is the WeCom digest forwarder; no kernel module build job in the repository

evidence.description: full harness output: pre-fix baseline, PR head baseline, residual case on PR head, residual case with the WAIT timeout guard
10 baseline sequences on the PR head FSM
same sequences on the main FSM, showing the bug
two sequences where a held key or the all-released gate leaves used set when the 300 ms timeout fires
same two sequences with the proposed timeout guard, ending IDLE layer=0
PR state, author, scope, base/head, commits, comments/reviews, checks
redacted local Device Service cardputer-zero profile fields

notes: Evidence class is host-level test plus code-level verification; no virtual-device or hardware run was possible on this host.
The residual WAIT+TIMEOUT+used window is pre-existing on main and strictly narrowed by this PR; it was reported as a non-blocking observation with a one-line proposal, not as a merge blocker.
No upstream branch was pushed, no PR was closed, and no other repository was modified; one English review comment was posted.
